newsitem.title: JAPAN: All TOCOM palladium futures surge by daily limits.
newsitem.headline: All TOCOM palladium futures surge by daily limits.

text.p: All yen-based palladium futures contracts on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) surged by their 36 yen per gram daily limit at the start of trade on Monday, following steep gains in New York last Friday, traders said.
The benchmark June palladium futures contract rose by its 36 yen per gram daily limit to 719 yen at the opening. Spot August palladium, which has no limit, started 70 yen per gram higher at 915 yen.
Platinum futures also opened higher in line with palladium, with the October platinum contract starting up by its 50 yen per gram price limit at 1,654. Limitless August rose by 102 yen to 1,745 yen.

"Tight physical PGMs supplies and lower-than-expected Russian spot sales after Russia resumed long-delayed exports prompted private investors to cover their massive short positions," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
The analyst said palladium futures are likely to be glued to their limit-up levels for most of the day.

Traders said the bullish trend is likely to continue despite rapid price gains in recent days, as the resumption of Russian exports has failed to dispel concern over the stability of Russian supplies.
Gold was narrowly mixed. Benchmark June was down one yen per gram at 1,228 yen in early Tokyo morning trade.
